Subject: Draft response to Peregrine redlines - SLA items

Hi Lauren, Kim —

Peregrine sent redlines on the order form and the SLA this morning. The three asks we need to address in our response are:

1) Uptime definition: they want a 99.95% uptime for the global API with a single aggregated monthly measurement (they've proposed removing region-level accountability).
2) Service credits: they're carving a larger credit band for any monthly availability below 99.95 and want an uncapped credit for consecutive monthly failures.
3) Maintenance windows: they want to limit planned maintenance to a single 6-hour annual blackout and disallow rolling blackouts longer than 30m per region.

Attached the redlined OrderForm (Peregrine_OrderForm_v2.docx) and my annotated SLA_Schedule_Proposal.xlsx. High-level thoughts: we can accept a 99.95% global target for Hosted API only if we keep region-level SLOs for Dedicated/Private; we should cap aggregate credits to the committed spend for the month and keep the rolling maintenance allowance (we rely on staggered 30–90m per-region windows to do safe upgrades). Also we should preserve our existing P1/P2 response-time ladder and keep the 4-hour P1 response on Dedicated.

Proposed next steps: I can send a clean redline that keeps a 99.95% global for hosted but preserves regional accountability for Dedicated/Private + capped credits. Lauren — can you thread legal in for the final wording? Kim — any ops concerns if we grant a single annual 6h blackout?

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick reply and for the annotated docs. A couple clarifications from our side:

• The request to measure availability at a global level stems from our multi-region traffic distribution — we need predictable behavior when a region is impacted.
• Uncapped consecutive-month credits are a sticking point for us because our risk models assume compensation if service stabilizes but also a means to compel rapid remediation.
• On maintenance windows: the ask for a single 6-hour annual blackout is driven by our compliance team — anything larger than that triggers a bespoke approval process on our end.

We are open to a compromise: keep a 99.95% global target but include regional thresholds that only trigger operational escalation (not credit) unless they cross 99.5% for two consecutive months. For credits, would Redwood consider a staircase model (3 tiers) with a monthly cap equal to 100% of the monthly subscription for a single month and a separate clause for consecutive months that requires an executive escape hatch rather than automatically uncapped credits?

Marcus

Jordan & Lauren —

Ops perspective: we cannot accept a single annual 6-hour blackout as our only maintenance allowance. Our upgrade cadence requires region-staggered windows to keep rolling restarts below user-impact thresholds. If we squeeze to a single 6h blackout it pushes more emergency changes into unplanned work.

Counterproposal from infra: permit one 6h annual blackout plus four annual regional windows (each up to 60 minutes) for major upgrades. The regional windows may be scheduled with 72h notice and will include pre-warm steps to minimize KV-cache miss penalties.

On the credits side: capping credits at 100% of monthly committed fees for any single month is reasonable, but we should ensure the definition of "monthly committed fees" excludes one-off services (professional services, data migration).

Kim
Director, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference

Marcus, Taylor —

Appreciate the open approach. Attached is a clean redline that reflects Redwood's compromise:

• Uptime: 99.95% global for Hosted API with explicit regional SLOs (99.9% region-level for Dedicated/Private). Regional failures trigger operational escalations and reporting; credits are calculated on the monthly global measurement.
• Credits: staircase model with three tiers. Each monthly incident is capped at 100% of that month's recurring subscription fees. Consecutive monthly failures require exec-level review and remediation plan; automatic uncapped credits are not included.
• Maintenance: one 6-hour annual blackout for major platform upgrades, plus up to four regional maintenance windows per year (max 60 minutes each) with 72h notice. Rolling restarts for safety (max 30 minutes per region) are permitted and documented in the maintenance plan.

Taylor — could you please confirm the legal phrasing for the consecutive-months clause (we want an "executive remediation review" path rather than an automatic escalator to uncapped credits). Also please confirm that the credit cap excludes non-recurring professional services.

Jordan/Kim — once Taylor gives wording we will send to Marcus for sign-off and then push to DocuSign.

Thanks,
